context: Proof The theorem by Fejes-Toth states that for the regular simplex T , there is a ball B such that 1 d B ⊆ T ⊆ B and hence B ⊆ dT . It also implies that if T is any simplex T in the ball, then if for scaling factor s we had T ⊆ B ⊆ x + sT then we would have: 1s (B − x) ⊆ T ⊆ B and hence s ≥ d. Even for d = 2, we do not know if this lower bound is tight. Question 6 For d = 2 is the circle the worst-case for John’s theorem for simplices? In other words, given any set X ∈ R2 , can you always find a triangle T with vertices in X so that X is contained in some translate of 2T ? Acknowledgments We would like to thank Allen Liu for reading an earlier version of this manuscript and pointing out to us that our approach in Section 3 results in an algorithm with total cost O(dc(ε/d)) (instead of O(dc(ε/d2 )), as we had originally written).
